name: Kora
shortDescription: 21-string West African harp-lute with calabash gourd resonator, cowskin soundboard, and notched bridge.
description: The kora is a 21-string West African chordophone played by the Jali (griot) caste across Gambia, Senegal, Mali, and Guinea. It combines features of the harp and the lute: strings run across a raised, notched bridge perpendicular to a cowhide sound table stretched over a large calabash gourd resonator. Played with thumb and index fingers of both hands, the kora produces intricate polyphonic ostinatos (kumbengo) and soaring vocal improvisations (birimintingo).
historicalOrigins: Originating in the Mandinka empire (Kaabu) along the Gambia River in the 16th century, the kora is the sacred instrument of oral historians, genealogists, and court musicians.
acousticPrinciples: Strings pass over notched wooden bridge resting perpendicularly on cowhide membrane table
String pluck excites bridge rocking motion, driving skin membrane with fast acoustic rise-time
Large half-calabash gourd functions as a natural Helmholtz acoustic chamber with side soundhole
Split string plane allows two hands to play independent polyrhythmic bass and treble lines simultaneously

characteristics.timbralColor: Sparkling, liquid, harp-like brilliance combined with guitar-like punch and warm gourd body resonance
characteristics.orchestralRole: Griot storytelling lead, polyrhythmic cyclical ostinatos (kumbengo), virtuosic soloing (birimintingo)

soundDNA.exciter: Thumbs and index finger nails plucking nylon / monofilament fishing line strings
soundDNA.resonator: Calabash gourd with stretched wet-cured cowhide soundboard and rosewood bridge
soundDNA.harmonics: Rich mid-high harmonics with quick transient spike and resonant low-end 'thump'
soundDNA.attackDecay: Snappy transient attack (<15 ms); moderate sustain (1.5 - 3.5s) in calabash body
soundDNA.timbreProfile: Cascade of crystalline plucks rooted in an organic woody, skin-driven cavity resonance
soundDNA.radiationPattern: Forward acoustic projection from skin table; warm hemispherical spread from calabash side port

calabash.label: Calabash Gourd (Resonator)
calabash.function: Large dried gourd sphere cut in half, providing structural acoustic bowl and Helmholtz chamber.

skin_table.label: Cowskin Sound Table
skin_table.function: Wet-stretched shaved cowhide tacked to the gourd lip, transmitting bridge vibrations to the chamber.

characteristics.material: Cured cowhide parchment fastened with chrome upholstery tacks

neck_stick.label: Hardwood Neck (Spike)
neck_stick.function: Straight hardwood pole passing completely through the gourd body to anchor strings and bridge.

characteristics.mechanism: Rigid structural spine resisting multi-string tension

bridge.label: Notched Rosewood Bridge
bridge.function: Stepped upright bridge separating 21 strings into two parallel vertical planes (11 left, 10 right).

characteristics.material: Hardwood padauk with leather base cushion
characteristics.mechanism: Rocking lever transmitting string tension to skin table

handposts.label: Handposts & Crossbar
handposts.function: Wooden handles gripped by the 3rd, 4th, and 5th fingers while thumbs and index fingers pluck.

characteristics.mechanism: Ergonomic anchor for two-handed polyrhythmic dexterity

strings.label: 21 Plucked Strings
strings.function: Monofilament strings tuned heptatonically in Silaba, Tomora, or Hardino scales.

characteristics.material: Modern nylon monofilament (formerly twisted antelope hide)

followTheSound.title: Dual-Hand Pluck
followTheSound.explanation: Player uses thumbs (downward bass plucks) and index fingers (upward treble plucks) on separate string planes.

followTheSound.title: Upright Bridge Levering
followTheSound.explanation: String vibration rocks the tall, upright bridge down into the center of the taught cowhide sound table.

followTheSound.title: Skin Membrane Excitation
followTheSound.explanation: The cowskin membrane flexes vigorously, projecting bright, punchy acoustic transient sound pressure.

followTheSound.title: Calabash Cavity Resonance
followTheSound.explanation: The deep spherical gourd reinforces fundamental warm lows, escaping through the side monitor port to the musician's ears.
